title: Site-comparison unit transports a given composition mate and its counits
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$, and put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gB$ be separated finite-type maps of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $h=f,g,gf$, choose a compactification with finite-dimensional ambient scheme [def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. On ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], put $F_h=Rh_{e,!}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], let $R_h$ be its ambient etale right adjoint, and assume $F_h,R_h$ preserve $D^+$. Suppose $\alpha:F_gF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{gf}$ is a specified natural isomorphism on $D^+$ and $\theta:R_{gf}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_fR_g$ is its right-adjoint mate, normalized by
$$\epsilon_{gf,H}\circ\alpha_{R_{gf}H}=\epsilon_{g,H}\circ F_g(\epsilon_{f,R_gH})\circ F_gF_f(\theta_H).$$
Here $\epsilon_h$ are the etale counits and $H\in D^+(B_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.

Write $S_T=\nu_T^*$, $U_T=R\nu_{T,*}$ and $\eta_T:\mathrm{id}\to U_TS_T$ for site comparison and its unit [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], and put $Q_h=S_{\mathrm{source}(h)}R_hU_{\mathrm{target}(h)}$, the finite exceptional comparison functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. For $J\in D^+(\mathrm{target}(h)_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ set
$$\rho_{h,J}=S_{\mathrm{source}(h)}R_h(\eta_{\mathrm{target}(h),J}):S_{\mathrm{source}(h)}R_hJ\longrightarrow Q_hS_{\mathrm{target}(h)}J.$$
These are natural isomorphisms between bounded-below objects. To specify the relative adjunction normalization, let $P_h$ be pro-etale compact support at the same compactification [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and for $G\in D^+(\mathrm{source}(h)_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ let $B_{h,G}:S_{\mathrm{target}(h)}F_hG\xrightarrow{\sim}P_hS_{\mathrm{source}(h)}G$ be the comparison $B_{f,G}$ of [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose] for $h$ and the chosen compactification, built from the proper direct-image and extension-by-zero site comparisons (its invertibility on etale-origin inputs is also [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]). The relative Hom bijection on $S_{\mathrm{source}(h)}G$, $G\in D^+$, with identity etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], is fixed to send $z:P_hS_{\mathrm{source}(h)}G\to N$ to
$$\Phi_{h;G,N}(z)=S_{\mathrm{source}(h)}\!\left(\operatorname{adj}_h\!\left(U_{\mathrm{target}(h)}(z\circ B_{h,G})\circ\eta_{\mathrm{target}(h),F_hG}\right)\right),$$
where $N\in D^+(\mathrm{target}(h)_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $\operatorname{adj}_h$ is the ordinary etale $F_h\dashv R_h$ transpose; this is the specified bijection of [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose]. Let $\mu_{h,N}:P_hQ_hN\to N$ be its relative counit (the inverse image of the identity at $Q_hN$, using its etale-origin witness), natural in $N$. For $J\in D^+(\mathrm{target}(h)_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ this normalization satisfies
$$\mu_{h,S_{\mathrm{target}(h)}J}\circ P_h(\rho_{h,J})\circ B_{h,R_hJ}=S_{\mathrm{target}(h)}(\epsilon_{h,J}).$$ The formula
$$\Xi_H=\rho_{gf,H}\circ S_X(\theta_H^{-1})\circ\rho_{f,R_gH}^{-1}\circ Q_f(\rho_{g,H}^{-1}):Q_fQ_gS_BH\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{gf}S_BH$$
defines a natural isomorphism on $D^+(B_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. It is the transported inverse composition mate in the following precise sense. For $G\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put
$$\alpha^p_G=B_{gf,G}\circ S_B(\alpha_G)\circ B_{g,F_fG}^{-1}\circ P_g(B_{f,G})^{-1}:P_gP_fS_XG\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{gf}S_XG.$$
Then for every $H\in D^+(B_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the transported pasted-counit identity
$$\mu_{gf,S_BH}\circ P_{gf}(\rho_{gf,H})\circ\alpha^p_{R_{gf}H}=\mu_{g,S_BH}\circ P_g(\mu_{f,Q_gS_BH})\circ P_gP_f\bigl(\Xi_H^{-1}\circ\rho_{gf,H}\bigr)$$
holds, both sides being maps $P_gP_fS_XR_{gf}H\to S_BH$. Thus the normalization refers to relative adjunctions on the comparison class, without requiring an adjunction on arbitrary pro-etale objects.

Let $A_e$ and $A_p$ denote the constant coefficient sheaves on $B$ in degree zero. Under the canonical scalar-preserving identification $S_BA_e\cong A_p$ of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] for $\nu_B$, put $\lambda_h=\rho_{h,A_e}$ for $h=g,gf$, with this identification on the target. At $H=A_e$ the same map is exactly
$$Q_fQ_gA_p\xrightarrow{Q_f(\lambda_g^{-1})}Q_fS_YR_gA_e\xrightarrow{\rho_{f,R_gA_e}^{-1}}S_XR_fR_gA_e\xrightarrow{S_X(\theta_{A_e}^{-1})}S_XR_{gf}A_e\xrightarrow{\lambda_{gf}}Q_{gf}A_p.$$

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6; agent-formulated comparison-unit transport of a given etale composition mate. Serves the first proof paragraph of cor-weil-boundary-duality-discharge, returned steps 6–7.

proof.text: By [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], the specified unit $\eta_{T,J}:J\to U_TS_TJ$ is a natural isomorphism for every $J\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Apply the functor $S_{\mathrm{source}(h)}R_h$ to it: its inverse is the image of $\eta_{T,J}^{-1}$, giving exactly $\rho_{h,J}^{-1}$. The source is bounded below because $R_h$ preserves $D^+$ by hypothesis and $S$ preserves $D^+$ by [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]; hence its isomorphic target is bounded below too. Naturality follows by applying this functor to the naturality square of $\eta$. In particular $R_gH$, $R_fR_gH$, $R_{gf}H$ and their $S$-images have the bounds needed below.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 (p. 35); agent-written formal composition-unit and relative-counit calculation, with the specified normalization of lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose] to each $h=f,g,gf$ at its specified compactification. Its $C,F_e,F_p,f^\times$ are respectively our $S,F_h,P_h,R_h$, and its displayed Hom bijection is exactly the $\Phi$ fixed in the statement, not a freely chosen adjunction. Its counit is therefore $\mu$. The hypotheses hold: the schemes are finite type over $k$, each map is separated finite type, each ambient dimension admits an integer upper bound, and $R_hJ\in D^+$ is assumed. It gives natural isomorphisms $B_{h,G}$ and the precise equality
$$\mu_{h,SJ}\circ P_h(\rho_{h,J})\circ B_{h,R_hJ}=S(\epsilon_{h,J}).$$
Both this equality and the naturality of $B$ will be used only on bounded-below etale inputs.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 (p. 35); agent-written formal composition-unit and relative-counit calculation, with the specified normalization of lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose.

proof.text:
Each of the four factors in the displayed definition of $\Xi_H$ is an isomorphism: the $\rho$ factors by step 1, $S_X(\theta_H^{-1})$ by the hypothesis on $\theta$, and the remaining factor because functors preserve inverse pairs. Their sources and targets concatenate as written in the statement. They are natural in $H$ (inverse naturality follows by multiplying a naturality square by the inverses), so their composite is a natural isomorphism. For later use put $K=R_{gf}H$, $L=R_fR_gH$, $t=\theta_H$, $r=\rho_{g,H}$, $b=\rho_{f,R_gH}$ and $v=\rho_{gf,H}$. Reversing the four factors and cancelling $v^{-1}v$ gives
$$\Xi_H^{-1}\circ v=Q_f(r)\circ b\circ S_X(t).$$

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 (p. 35); agent-written formal composition-unit and relative-counit calculation, with the specified normalization of lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose.

proof.text:
The same inverse-pair and naturality argument applied to $B_{gf,G}$, $S_B(\alpha_G)$, $B_{g,F_fG}^{-1}$ and $P_g(B_{f,G})^{-1}$ proves that the stated $\alpha^p_G$ is a natural isomorphism. Here $F_fG\in D^+$ by hypothesis. Applying the step-2 counit equality at $gf$ and substituting the four-factor definition of $\alpha^p$ shows that the left side of the desired identity is
$$S_B(\epsilon_{gf,H}\circ\alpha_K)\circ B_{g,F_fK}^{-1}\circ P_g(B_{f,K}^{-1}).$$
This uses only associativity, functoriality and $B_{gf,K}^{-1}B_{gf,K}=1$.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 (p. 35); agent-written formal composition-unit and relative-counit calculation, with the specified normalization of lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose.

proof.text:
Expand the right side using step 3. Naturality of the given relative counit $\mu_f:P_fQ_f\to\mathrm{id}$ at $r:S_YR_gH\to Q_gS_BH$ says
$$\mu_{f,Q_gS_BH}\circ P_fQ_f(r)=r\circ\mu_{f,S_YR_gH}.$$
Thus that side becomes
$$\mu_{g,S_BH}\circ P_g(r)\circ P_g(\mu_{f,S_YR_gH}\circ P_f(b))\circ P_gP_f(S_X(t)).$$
The two targets of the naturality square are bounded below by step 1, so the assumed naturality of the relative counit applies.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 (p. 35); agent-written formal composition-unit and relative-counit calculation, with the specified normalization of lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose.

proof.text:
In the expression of step 5, use step 2 for $g$ at $H$ and for $f$ at $R_gH$, cancelling the respective invertible $B$ factors on the right. The result is
$$S_B(\epsilon_{g,H})\circ B_{g,R_gH}^{-1}\circ P_g(S_Y(\epsilon_{f,R_gH}))\circ P_g(B_{f,L}^{-1})\circ P_gP_f(S_X(t)).$$
All arguments of $B$ and of the etale counits here are bounded below by the assumptions on $F_h,R_h$.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 (p. 35); agent-written formal composition-unit and relative-counit calculation, with the specified normalization of lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose.

proof.text:
Use the following three inverse-naturality equations, in the indicated order, in step 6:
$$B_{g,R_gH}^{-1}\circ P_g(S_Y\epsilon_{f,R_gH})=S_B(F_g\epsilon_{f,R_gH})\circ B_{g,F_fL}^{-1},$$
$$B_{f,L}^{-1}\circ P_f(S_Xt)=S_Y(F_ft)\circ B_{f,K}^{-1},$$
$$B_{g,F_fL}^{-1}\circ P_g(S_YF_ft)=S_B(F_gF_ft)\circ B_{g,F_fK}^{-1}.$$
Each is the naturality square for $B_h:SF_h\to P_hS$ at, respectively, $\epsilon_{f,R_gH}$, $t$, and $F_ft$, multiplied by the two inverse $B$ components. Functoriality and associativity now give for the right side
$$S_B(\epsilon_{g,H}\circ F_g(\epsilon_{f,R_gH})\circ F_gF_f(t))\circ B_{g,F_fK}^{-1}\circ P_g(B_{f,K}^{-1}).$$

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 (p. 35); agent-written formal composition-unit and relative-counit calculation, with the specified normalization of lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose.

proof.text:
The assumed etale mate normalization says precisely
$$\epsilon_{g,H}\circ F_g(\epsilon_{f,R_gH})\circ F_gF_f(t)=\epsilon_{gf,H}\circ\alpha_K.$$
Substitution into step 7 gives the expression in step 4. This proves the displayed pasted-counit identity as an equality of maps from $P_gP_fS_XK$ to $S_BH$. Every occurrence of $\mu$ above has a bounded-below target and the $Q$-object is of etale origin; no adjunction on arbitrary pro-etale objects was used.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 (p. 35); agent-written formal composition-unit and relative-counit calculation, with the specified normalization of lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose.

proof.text: The degree-zero constant sheaf $A_e$ is bounded below. By [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], inverse image for $\nu_B$ identifies $S_BA_e$ with $A_p$, preserving every scalar, and the identification is also valid termwise on derived categories. Specialize the four factors of $\Xi_H$ to $H=A_e$. Then $\rho_{g,A_e}=\lambda_g$ and $\rho_{gf,A_e}=\lambda_{gf}$ by definition; the middle two factors are unchanged. This is exactly the four-arrow composite in the last clause. The identity already proved specializes with it.
